```yaml
name: nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 3 * * *"   # 03:00 UTC daily
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: nightly
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: "1"
  PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK: "1"
  GRADLE_OPTS: "-Dorg.gradle.daemon=false"

jobs:
  complex-corpus:
    name: parity complex
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
      - run: ./scripts/ci_setup.sh
      - run: |
          source .venv/bin/activate
          OARUMI_STRICT_PARITY=1 pytest tests/parity -q \
            --parity-corpus=parity-complex \
            --timeout=120
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: parity-complex-results
          path: tests/parity/reports/
          retention-days: 14

  chaos:
    name: chaos recovery
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
      - run: ./scripts/ci_setup.sh
      - run: |
          source .venv/bin/activate
          pytest tests/chaos -q --timeout=300 -p no:cacheprovider
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: chaos-failure-artifacts
          path: |
            tests/chaos/reports/
            .oarumi-audit.jsonl
          retention-days: 14

  bench:
    name: benchmarks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
      - run: ./scripts/ci_setup.sh
      - run: |
          source .venv/bin/activate
          pytest tests/bench -q --benchmark-only \
            --benchmark-json=bench-report.json \
            --timeout=300
      - name: Compare to baseline
        run: |
          source .venv/bin/activate
          python tools/bench_compare.py \
            --current bench-report.json \
            --baseline tests/bench/baseline.json \
            --tolerance 1.20
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bench-report
          path: bench-report.json
          retention-days: 30

  android-instrumented:
    name: android instrumented
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"
      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
      - run: ./scripts/ci_setup.sh
      - name: Enable KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' \
            | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      - name: Run instrumented tests on emulator
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 34
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          script: |
            cd android
            ./gradlew --no-daemon :app:connectedMlkitDebugAndroidTest
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: android-instrumented-reports
          path: android/app/build/reports/androidTests/
          retention-days: 14

  parity-web-e2e:
    name: parity web e2e
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
      - run: ./scripts/ci_setup.sh
      - name: Start server
        run: |
          source .venv/bin/activate
          nohup python -m tools.parity_web.server > /tmp/parity-web.log 2>&1 &
          echo $! > /tmp/parity-web.pid
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health >/dev/null; then exit 0; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          echo "server did not start"
          cat /tmp/parity-web.log
          exit 1
      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          source .venv/bin/activate
          curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/ | grep -q "Oarumi Parity"
          curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/static/app.js | grep -q "window.Oarumi"
          curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/static/diff.js | grep -q "render"
          curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/static/failover.js | grep -q "render"
          echo "shell + assets OK"
      - name: Trigger a small run and poll it
        run: |
          source .venv/bin/activate
          RUN=$(curl -sf -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/runs \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            -d '{"corpus":"parity-basic","targets":["python"]}')
          RUN_ID=$(echo "$RUN" | python -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['run_id'])")
          for i in $(seq 1 120); do
            STATUS=$(curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/runs/$RUN_ID | python -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['status'])")
            if [ "$STATUS" = "done" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "failed" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "partial" ]; then
              echo "run $RUN_ID finished with status=$STATUS"
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
          echo "run did not finish within 120s"
          curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/runs/$RUN_ID | python -m json.tool
          exit 1
      - name: Fetch diff
        run: |
          source .venv/bin/activate
          curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/diff/$RUN_ID | python -m json.tool | head -40
      - name: Stop server
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ -f /tmp/parity-web.pid ]; then
            kill "$(cat /tmp/parity-web.pid)" || true
            cat /tmp/parity-web.log | tail -100
          fi

  nightly-pass:
    name: nightly-pass
    needs: [complex-corpus, chaos, bench, android-instrumented, parity-web-e2e]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check all jobs
        run: |
          failed=""
          for result in \
            "${{ needs.complex-corpus.result }}" \
            "${{ needs.chaos.result }}" \
            "${{ needs.bench.result }}" \
            "${{ needs.android-instrumented.result }}" \
            "${{ needs.parity-web-e2e.result }}"; do
            if [[ "$result" != "success" ]]; then failed="yes"; fi
          done
          if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
            echo "One or more nightly jobs failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All nightly jobs passed"
```

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def repo_root() -> Path:
    return ROOT

def bench_db():
    from oarumi.db import LanguageDb
    path = ROOT / "language" / "oarumi.db"
    if not path.exists():
        pytest.skip("language DB missing; run ./scripts/bootstrap.sh")
    return LanguageDb(path)


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def bench_pipeline(bench_db):
    from oarumi.config import EngineConfig
    from oarumi.pipeline import Pipeline
    from oarumi.renderers.audio_assets import AudioAssetLibrary
    from oarumi.renderers.sign import HamNoSysToSigML, SignRenderer
    from oarumi.renderers.tactile import TactileRenderer
    from oarumi.renderers.tts import TtsRenderer

    cfg = EngineConfig.from_env()
    pipeline = Pipeline(db=bench_db, cfg=cfg)

        pipeline.register_renderer("spoken", lambda s: tts.render(s).to_json())

    sign = SignRenderer(converter=HamNoSysToSigML(use_external=False))
    pipeline.register_renderer("signed", lambda s: sign.render(s).to_json())
    pipeline.register_renderer("tactile", lambda s: TactileRenderer().render(s).to_json())
    return pipeline

from __future__ import annotations

from oarumi.types import TranslationRequest


@pytest.mark.benchmark(group="pipeline")

    result = benchmark(bench_pipeline.translate, req)

def test_translate_signed_modality(benchmark, bench_pipeline) -> None:
    req = TranslationRequest(text="hola", lang="es", modality="signed")
    result = benchmark(bench_pipeline.translate, req)

@pytest.mark.benchmark(group="pipeline")

    result = benchmark(bench_pipeline.translate, req)
    assert result.modalities.get("tactile")


@pytest.mark.benchmark(group="pipeline")
def test_translate_degraded_path(benchmark, bench_pipeline) -> None:

    result = benchmark(bench_pipeline.translate, req)

@pytest.mark.benchmark(group="nsm")
def test_decompose_tier_a(benchmark, bench_db) -> None:
    from oarumi.nsm.decomposer import NSMDecomposerTierA
    dec = NSMDecomposerTierA(bench_db)
    nsm = benchmark(dec.decompose, "I want water")
    assert nsm.valid


@pytest.mark.benchmark(group="nsm")
def test_realize(benchmark, bench_db) -> None:
    from oarumi.nsm.decomposer import NSMDecomposerTierA
    from oarumi.nsm.realizer import NSMRealizer
    dec = NSMDecomposerTierA(bench_db)
    rea = NSMRealizer(bench_db)
    nsm = dec.decompose("I want water")
    surface = benchmark(rea.realize, nsm)
    assert surface.phonemes


@pytest.mark.benchmark(group="reliability")
def test_shield_valid_path(benchmark, tmp_path) -> None:
    from oarumi.reliability.audit_log import AuditLog
    from oarumi.reliability.symbolic_shield import ParityContract, SymbolicShield
    from oarumi.types import ValidationOutcome
    shield = SymbolicShield(audit=AuditLog(tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"))
    call = shield.wrap(
        component="x",
        neural=lambda _: "ok",
        validator=lambda _: ValidationOutcome(valid=True),
        fallback=lambda _: "fb",
        contract=ParityContract(validity_required=True, latency_ceiling_ms=1000),
    )
    r = benchmark(call, 1)
    assert r.decision == "use_neural"


@pytest.mark.benchmark(group="reliability")
def test_shield_fallback_path(benchmark, tmp_path) -> None:
    from oarumi.reliability.audit_log import AuditLog
    from oarumi.reliability.symbolic_shield import ParityContract, SymbolicShield
    from oarumi.types import ValidationOutcome
    shield = SymbolicShield(audit=AuditLog(tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"))
    call = shield.wrap(
        component="x",
        neural=lambda _: "bad",
        validator=lambda _: ValidationOutcome(valid=False, errors=("bad",)),
        fallback=lambda _: "fb",
        contract=ParityContract(validity_required=True, latency_ceiling_ms=1000),
    )
    r = benchmark(call, 1)
    assert r.decision == "use_fallback"

## `tools/bench_compare.py`

```python
"""Compare pytest-benchmark output against a baseline JSON file.

    python tools/bench_compare.py --current bench-report.json \
      --baseline tests/bench/baseline.json --tolerance 1.20

Exits non-zero if any benchmark's mean exceeds baseline * tolerance.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def _load_current(path: Path) -> dict[str, float]:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    out: dict[str, float] = {}
    for bench in data.get("benchmarks", []):
        name = bench["name"].rsplit("::", 1)[-1]
        mean_s = bench["stats"]["mean"]
        out[name] = mean_s * 1000.0
    return out


def _load_baseline(path: Path) -> dict[str, float]:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return {b["name"]: float(b["mean_ms"]) for b in data.get("benchmarks", [])}


def compare(current_path: Path, baseline_path: Path, tolerance: float) -> int:
    current = _load_current(current_path)
    baseline = _load_baseline(baseline_path)

    if not baseline:
        print("WARN baseline empty; skipping comparison", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0

    regressions: list[str] = []
    missing_baseline: list[str] = []
    missing_current: list[str] = []

    for name, base in baseline.items():
        if name not in current:
            missing_current.append(name)
            continue
        cur = current[name]
        limit = base * tolerance
        if cur > limit:
            regressions.append(
                f"{name}: current={cur:.2f}ms baseline={base:.2f}ms "
                f"limit={limit:.2f}ms (ratio={cur / base:.2f}×)"
            )

    for name in current:
        if name not in baseline:
            missing_baseline.append(name)

    for name in missing_current:
        print(f"MISSING current: {name}", file=sys.stderr)
    for name in missing_baseline:
        print(f"NOTE new benchmark: {name} (add to baseline after review)")

    if regressions:
        for r in regressions:
            print(f"REGRESSION {r}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print(f"OK   {len(baseline)} benchmarks within {tolerance:.0%} tolerance")
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--current", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--baseline", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--tolerance", type=float, default=1.20)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    return compare(args.current, args.baseline, args.tolerance)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

## `tests/chaos/test_recovery_chaos.py`

```python
"""Chaos tests. Exercise the recovery FSM under adversarial triggers.

Run nightly (slow, probabilistic). Each test uses a fixed seed for
reproducibility.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
import time

import pytest

from oarumi.reliability.recovery_fsm import FSMState, RecoveryFSM


@pytest.mark.chaos
def test_random_trigger_sequence_reaches_consistent_state(rng: random.Random) -> None:
    """Feed random triggers; FSM must always end in a valid state and history
    must be internally consistent."""
    for _ in range(200):
        fsm = RecoveryFSM(component="chaos")
        for _ in range(50):
            op = rng.choice(["trigger", "canary_pass", "canary_fail", "rollback"])
            if op == "trigger":
                fsm.on_trigger(rng.choice(["a", "b", "c"]))
            elif op == "canary_pass":
                fsm.on_canary_pass()
            elif op == "canary_fail":
                if fsm.state == FSMState.RECOVERING:
                    fsm.on_canary_fail()
            elif op == "rollback":
                fsm.on_rollback()
        # Invariant: history transitions form a contiguous chain.
        for i in range(1, len(fsm.history)):
            assert fsm.history[i - 1].to == fsm.history[i].from
        # Invariant: last transition's `to` equals state.
        if fsm.history:
            assert fsm.history[-1].to == fsm.state


@pytest.mark.chaos
def test_canary_reentry_under_repeated_failures(fast_watchdog) -> None:
    """Simulate a flapping neural path: the FSM must not spin indefinitely.

    Backoff must prevent re-entry within a short interval after a failure.
    """
    wd, fired = fast_watchdog
    fsm = RecoveryFSM(component="chaos-flap")
    for _ in range(20):
        fsm.on_trigger("validation")
        # Handle the case where we're stuck in FAILED.
        if fsm.state == FSMState.FAILED:
            fsm.on_rollback()
    # After 20 trigger cycles we should not have entered RECOVERING more than 20 times.
    recover_entries = sum(1 for t in fsm.history if t.to == FSMState.RECOVERING)
    assert recover_entries <= 20


@pytest.mark.chaos
def test_watchdog_does_not_drift_under_load(fast_watchdog) -> None:
    """Arm and complete many handles in a tight loop; the fired list must
    reflect only actual timeouts."""
    wd, fired = fast_watchdog
    for i in range(500):
        h = wd.arm(f"c{i}", deadline_s=0.2)
        wd.completed(h)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    assert fired == [], f"unexpected timeouts: {len(fired)}"


@pytest.mark.chaos
def test_simultaneous_watchdog_timeout_and_completion(fast_watchdog) -> None:
    """Race a timeout against a late completion; the handle must be marked
    fired exactly once (or completed, but not both)."""
    wd, fired = fast_watchdog
    handles = []
    for i in range(50):
        h = wd.arm(f"c{i}", deadline_s=0.01)
        handles.append(h)
    time.sleep(0.05)  # let some fire
    for h in handles:
        wd.completed(h)
    time.sleep(0.05)
    # Fired handles must be marked fired; non-fired ones must be marked done.
    for h in handles:
        assert h.is_fired() or h.is_done()
        assert not (h.is_fired() and not h.is_done())  # once fired, cannot be un-done


@pytest.mark.chaos
def test_audit_log_survives_repeated_rotation(tmp_path) -> None:
    """Force many rotations; replay must still produce a well-formed event stream."""
    from oarumi.reliability.audit_log import AuditLog
    log = AuditLog(tmp_path / "audit.jsonl", max_bytes=200)
    for i in range(500):
        log.log_simple("chaos", "event", i=i)
    events = log.replay()
    assert len(events) >= 500
    # Every line must be valid JSON (replay drops invalid ones, so count alone
    # proves the log didn't corrupt).
    assert all(e.event == "event" for e in events)


@pytest.mark.chaos
def test_shield_under_mixed_valid_invalid_traffic(tmp_path, rng) -> None:
    """Send a mix of valid and invalid neural outputs; every decision must be
    recorded and consistent with the parity contract."""
    from oarumi.reliability.audit_log import AuditLog
    from oarumi.reliability.symbolic_shield import ParityContract, SymbolicShield
    from oarumi.types import ValidationOutcome

    log = AuditLog(tmp_path / "audit.jsonl")
    shield = SymbolicShield(audit=log)
    call = shield.wrap(
        component="chaos",
        neural=lambda x: x,
        validator=lambda x: ValidationOutcome(valid=x["valid"]),
        fallback=lambda _: {"valid": True, "source": "fallback"},
        contract=ParityContract(validity_required=True, latency_ceiling_ms=1000),
    )
    decisions: list[str] = []
    for _ in range(200):
        valid = rng.random() > 0.5
        r = call({"valid": valid})
        decisions.append(r.decision)
    events = [e for e in log.replay() if e.event == "shield_decision"]
    assert len(events) == 200
    assert decisions.count("use_neural") > 0
    assert decisions.count("use_fallback") > 0
```

## `docs/CI.md`

```markdown
# CI — Continuous Integration

Every PR runs `ci.yml`; nightly runs `nightly.yml`; tag pushes run
`android-release.yml` (Batch 12). This document explains the matrix and how
to reproduce a failure locally.

---

## § 1. Job overview

### PR jobs (`ci.yml`)

| Job | What it verifies | Typical duration |
|---|---|---|
| `lint` | `ruff`, `black --check`, `mypy --strict` on `engine/python`, `desktop`, `tools` | 2 min |
| `docs` | Every markdown link in the repo resolves | 30 s |
| `schema` | No drift between `language/*.yaml` and `language/schemas/*.json` | 30 s |
| `unit` (3.11, 3.12) | `engine/python/tests`, `desktop/tests`, `tools/tests` with `--cov-fail-under=85` | 6 min |
| `parity` | `tests/parity` (basic corpus) with `OARUMI_STRICT_PARITY=1` | 5 min |
| `fault` | `tests/fault` — every shield trigger fires | 3 min |
| `offline` | `tests/offline` — zero network calls | 3 min |
| `android-unit` | `:engine:test`, `:app:testMlkitDebugUnitTest`, `:app:testArgosDebugUnitTest` | 15 min |
| `parity-web` | `tools/parity_web/tests` with `--cov-fail-under=85` | 4 min |
| `ci-pass` | Aggregates the above; required status check | 10 s |

### Nightly jobs (`nightly.yml`)

| Job | What it verifies |
|---|---|
| `complex-corpus` | `tests/parity --parity-corpus=parity-complex` (slow) |
| `chaos` | `tests/chaos` — recovery FSM under random triggers |
| `bench` | `tests/bench --benchmark-only` compared to `tests/bench/baseline.json` (20% tolerance) |
| `android-instrumented` | `:app:connectedMlkitDebugAndroidTest` on an emulator |
| `parity-web-e2e` | Start the parity web server, curl health, trigger a real run, fetch the diff |

---

## § 2. Reproduce a failure locally

Every CI job is reproducible locally by running the same commands.

### `lint` fails

```bash
ruff check .
black --check .
mypy --strict engine/python desktop tools
ruff check --fix .      # auto-fix if possible
black .                 # reformat
```

### `docs` fails

```bash
python -m pytest tools/tests/test_docs_links.py -q
```

The failure message names the file and the broken link target.

### `schema` fails

```bash
python tools/schema_export.py --check
```

If drift is intentional:
1. Update `language/schemas/*.json` to declare the new field.
2. Add a migration in `language/migrations/` if the DB schema changed.
3. Re-run `python tools/validate_schemas.py --all` and `python tools/seed_db.py`.

### `unit` fails

```bash
./scripts/ci_setup.sh
source .venv/bin/activate
pytest engine/python/tests desktop/tests tools/tests -q \
  --cov=oarumi --cov=desktop --cov=tools --cov-fail-under=85
```

### `parity` fails

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
OARUMI_STRICT_PARITY=1 pytest tests/parity -q --parity-corpus=parity-basic
```

Read `tests/parity/README.md`. A parity failure is a **high-risk change** —
either the Python engine changed (and Kotlin must follow in the same PR) or
the frozen gold needs regeneration (`python tools/freeze_gold.py
--corpus parity-basic`, then review the diff).

### `fault` fails

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
pytest tests/fault -q
```

Look for the trigger in `tests/parity/config.yaml#fault_triggers` — every
trigger must have a passing test. A failure here means the shield or FSM
regressed.

### `offline` fails

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
pytest tests/offline -q -x
```

The `-x` stops at the first failure. The traceback shows the exact network
call that was attempted. Grep for `urllib`, `requests`, `http.client`,
`aiohttp`.

### `android-unit` fails

```bash
cd android
./gradlew --no-daemon :engine:test :app:testMlkitDebugUnitTest :app:testArgosDebugUnitTest
```

Test reports live at `android/engine/build/reports/tests/test/` and
`android/app/build/reports/tests/`.

### `parity-web` fails

```bash
python -m pytest tools/parity_web/tests -q --cov=tools.parity_web --cov-fail-under=85
```

---

## § 3. Nightly triage

Nightly failures are not PR-blocking but must be fixed within 48 hours.

### `bench` regression

Open `bench-report.json` and compare to `tests/bench/baseline.json`. A
regression is `current_mean_ms > baseline_mean_ms * 1.20`. To accept a new
baseline:

1. Confirm the regression is intentional (e.g., a new feature).
2. Replace `tests/bench/baseline.json` with the new means, reviewed line by
   line in the PR.
3. Note the change in `CHANGELOG.md`.

### `chaos` failure

The traceback shows the seeded random sequence. Reproduce with:

```bash
pytest tests/chaos -q -p no:cacheprovider
```

The `.oarumi-audit.jsonl` artifact contains the audit log from the failed
run. Look for the FSM transition sequence immediately before the assertion
fired.

### `android-instrumented` failure

Download `android-instrumented-reports` and open `index.html` in the
`connected/` subdirectory. It contains screenshots and logcat for failed
tests. Reproduce locally with a running emulator:

```bash
adb devices
cd android
./gradlew :app:connectedMlkitDebugAndroidTest
```

### `parity-web-e2e` failure

The server log is uploaded as `/tmp/parity-web.log`. Reproduce locally:

```bash
python -m tools.parity_web.server &
sleep 2
curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health
curl -sf -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/runs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"corpus":"parity-basic","targets":["python"]}'
```

## § 4. Caches and artifacts

| Cache | Key | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| pip | `requirements-lock.txt` + `pyproject.toml` | Avoid reinstalling deps |
| Gradle | `~/.gradle/caches`, `~/.gradle/wrapper` | Avoid re-downloading Gradle distribution |
| Android emulator | Not cached | Emulator is provisioned per nightly run |

Artifacts uploaded per PR:

- `coverage-py{311,312}.xml` (from `unit`)
- `parity-py-failure/` (only on parity failure)
- `android-test-results/` (from `android-unit`)

Artifacts uploaded per nightly:

- `parity-complex-results/`
- `chaos-failure-artifacts/`
- `bench-report/`
- `android-instrumented-reports/`

Retention: 7 days for PR, 14–30 days for nightly.

---

## § 5. Adding a new CI job

1. If it runs on every PR, add it to `ci.yml` and to the `needs` list of
   `ci-pass`.
2. If it runs nightly, add it to `nightly.yml` and to the `needs` list of
   `nightly-pass`.
3. If it has a coverage floor, use `--cov-fail-under=<N>`. Never allow a job
   to pass without a coverage floor if it is testing Python code.
4. Update this document's § 1 table and § 2 reproduction section.
5. Update `HANDOVER.md` § 6 (runbooks) if the job corresponds to a release
   step.

---

## § 6. Secret management

| Secret | Used by | Rotation |
|---|---|---|
| `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_B64` | `android-release.yml` | Only with store coordination |
| `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` | `android-release.yml` | Annually |
| `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS` | `android-release.yml` | Never (keystore continuity) |
| `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` | `android-release.yml` | Annually |
| `CODECOV_TOKEN` (optional) | None (coverage is uploaded as an artifact today) | N/A |

Secrets are provisioned at the org level. No CI job reads personal tokens.

### 0.1 `docs/PARITY_API.md` is now **generated**, not hand-maintained

The old hand-written version from Batch 1 is superseded. Delete the header note `> Generated by tools/schema_export.py (Batch 6)` from it and replace with the version in § 5 below. Add `tools/gen_parity_api.py` so it can be regenerated.

### 0.2 `tools/gen_parity_api.py`

```python
"""Generate docs/PARITY_API.md by inspecting the Python and Kotlin engines.

    python tools/gen_parity_api.py             # write the file
    python tools/gen_parity_api.py --check     # exit 1 if the file is stale

The Python side is introspected from types and signatures. The Kotlin side
is read from source files (grep for public fun / public class).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import inspect
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "docs" / "PARITY_API.md"
KT_SRC = ROOT / "engine" / "kotlin" / "src" / "main" / "kotlin" / "oarumi"


# --- Python side -------------------------------------------------------

PY_CLASSES = [
    "oarumi.db.LanguageDb",
    "oarumi.pivot.translator.PivotTranslator",
    "oarumi.nsm.decomposer.NSMDecomposerTierA",
    "oarumi.nsm.realizer.NSMRealizer",
    "oarumi.nsm.validator.NSMValidator",
    "oarumi.pipeline.Pipeline",
    "oarumi.reliability.intent_router.IntentRouter",
    "oarumi.reliability.symbolic_shield.SymbolicShield",
    "oarumi.reliability.recovery_fsm.RecoveryFSM",
    "oarumi.renderers.tts.TtsRenderer",
    "oarumi.renderers.sign.SignRenderer",
    "oarumi.renderers.tactile.TactileRenderer",
]


def _py_signatures() -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Return [(class_name, method, signature)] for the public surface."""
    import importlib

    rows: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    for dotted in PY_CLASSES:
        mod_path, cls_name = dotted.rsplit(".", 1)
        try:
            mod = importlib.import_module(mod_path)
        except ImportError:
            rows.append((dotted, "<import failed>", "<import failed>"))
            continue
        cls = getattr(mod, cls_name, None)
        if cls is None:
            continue
        for name, method in inspect.getmembers(cls, predicate=inspect.isfunction):
            if name.startswith("_"):
                continue
            try:
                sig = str(inspect.signature(method))
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                sig = "(?)"
            rows.append((cls_name, name, sig))
    return rows


# --- Kotlin side -------------------------------------------------------

_KT_CLASS_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:public\s+)?(?:data\s+|open\s+|abstract\s+)?class\s+(\w+)")
_KT_FUN_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:public\s+)?(?:suspend\s+)?fun\s+(?:<[^>]+>\s+)?(\w+)\s*\(")


def _kt_signatures() -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Return [(class_name, method, signature_placeholder)] for the public surface."""
    rows: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    if not KT_SRC.exists():
        return rows
    for path in sorted(KT_SRC.rglob("*.kt")):
        current_class = None
        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            m_cls = _KT_CLASS_RE.match(line)
            if m_cls:
                current_class = m_cls.group(1)
                continue
            m_fun = _KT_FUN_RE.match(line)
            if m_fun and current_class:
                name = m_fun.group(1)
                if name == current_class or name.startswith("_"):
                    continue
                rows.append((current_class, name, "(see source)"))
    return rows


# --- Rendering ---------------------------------------------------------

def _render() -> str:
    py = _py_signatures()
    kt = _kt_signatures()

    lines: list[str] = []
    lines.append("# Parity API — Cross-Language Contract\n")
    lines.append(
        "> **Generated file.** Do not edit by hand. Regenerate with "
        "`python tools/gen_parity_api.py`. The generator is checked by "
        "`--check` in CI; a stale file fails the `docs` job.\n"
    )
    lines.append(
        "The Python and Kotlin engines must expose identical public behavior on "
        "the deterministic path (ADR-0007). This file lists the public surface of "
        "each. Any method listed in one language but not the other is a bug; see "
        "`tests/parity/test_api_parity.py`.\n"
    )

    lines.append("\n## Python (`engine/python/oarumi/`)\n")
    lines.append("| Class | Method | Signature |")
    lines.append("|---|---|---|")
    for cls, name, sig in py:
        lines.append(f"| `{cls}` | `{name}` | `{sig}` |")

    lines.append("\n## Kotlin (`engine/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/oarumi/`)\n")
    lines.append("| Class | Method | Signature |")
    lines.append("|---|---|---|")
    for cls, name, sig in kt:
        lines.append(f"| `{cls}` | `{name}` | `{sig}` |")

    lines.append("\n## Equality rule\n")
    lines.append(
        "For every case in `tests/parity/data/parity-basic/`, the JSON produced by "
        "`Pipeline.translate` must be **byte-identical** between Python and Kotlin "
        "after canonical serialization (sorted keys, no whitespace, ephemeral fields "
        "stripped per `tools/parity_runner._canonical`). See ADR-0007.\n"
    )

    lines.append("\n## How this list is generated\n")
    lines.append(
        "- **Python**: `inspect.getmembers` over each public class; methods "
        "starting with `_` are excluded.\n"
        "- **Kotlin**: regex over `*.kt` source files; `public fun` and `suspend "
        "fun` are included; constructors and private methods are excluded.\n"
        "- Regenerated on every PR by the `docs` CI job via `--check`.\n"
    )

    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true",
                        help="Exit 1 if the checked-in file is stale")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    content = _render()
    if args.check:
        if not OUT.exists():
            print(f"FAIL missing {OUT}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        if OUT.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != content:
            print(f"FAIL {OUT} is stale; run `python tools/gen_parity_api.py`",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print(f"OK   {OUT} is up to date")
        return 0

    OUT.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"OK   wrote {OUT} ({len(content)} bytes)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

## 3. Critical dependencies and their risk

| Dependency | Role | Risk if unavailable | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| NSM prime inventory (Goddard & Wierzbicka 2014) | Semantic core | Language loses its universal foundation | Frozen copy in `language/primes.yaml`; citation in NOTICE |
| ML Kit on-device translation | Android pivot translation (mlkit flavor) | Android loses offline pivot for non-seed languages | `argos` flavor ships phrasebook-only; no runtime crash |
| Argos Translate | Desktop pivot translation | Desktop loses offline pivot for non-seed languages | Phrasebook fallback + structured degradation notice |
| CWASA / SiGML | Signed modality rendering | Signed modality unavailable | Pre-rendered symbol chips in WebView; avatar disabled in degraded mode |
| Whisper ggml | ASR front-end | Spoken input unavailable | Text input always available; app remains functional |
| eSpeak NG (desktop) | Desktop TTS | Desktop spoken output degraded | Asset backend is deterministic and always available |
| Android `TextToSpeech` | Android TTS | Android spoken output degraded | Asset backend handles clicks/hums; TTS unavailability shows a badge in the wizard |
| `sqlite-jdbc` | Kotlin JVM DB | JVM tests fail | Pinned version; `androidx.room` used on Android |

## 4. Where things live

- **Language definition** → `language/` (source of truth; all apps read this)
- **Python engine** → `engine/python/oarumi/`
- **Kotlin engine** → `engine/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/oarumi/`
- **Desktop app** → `desktop/`
- **Android app** → `android/app/src/`
- **Model manifests & training** → `models/`
- **Parity corpora & gold** → `tests/parity/data/` (generated; not committed)
- **Parity runner** → `tools/parity_runner.py`, `tools/parity_compare.py`
- **Parity web GUI** → `tools/parity_web/`
- **Architecture decisions** → `docs/adr/`
- **Generated parity API** → `docs/PARITY_API.md` (via `tools/gen_parity_api.py`)
- **Name clearance record** → `docs/NAME.md`
- **CI documentation** → `docs/CI.md`
- **Release checklist** → `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`
- **Roadmap** → `PLAN.md`
- **Task backlog** → `TODO.md`

## 5. Decisions that must not be silently reversed

These are load-bearing architectural commitments. To change any, open an ADR
and get sign-off from two maintainers.

1. **Pivot-and-NSM translation pipeline** (ADR-0001). Direct language pairs
   are not added; all translation routes through NSM.
2. **Tri-modal architecture** (ADR-0002). Spoken, signed, and tactile are
   first-class renderers of the same NSM structure.
3. **On-device inference only after bootstrap** (ADR-0003). No runtime cloud
   dependency is permitted.
4. **Deterministic failover for every neural component** (ADR-0004). A neural
   component without a parity-tested fallback cannot ship.
5. **Analytic/agglutinative core.** No fusional or polysynthetic core grammar.
6. **The name is Oarumi** (ADR-0005). It is an original coinage. Never
   "improve" it into a Latin or Greek derivative.
7. **Kotlin engine is a bit-exact port of Python** (ADR-0007). Any
   divergence on the deterministic path is a bug in Kotlin, not an acceptable
   platform difference.
8. **The parity web GUI is a first-class verification surface** (ADR-0006).
   It is not a dashboard; it is how humans and agents inspect the reliability
   contract.

## 6. Runbooks

### 6.1 Release a new version

See `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` for the full procedure. Summary:

1. Update `CHANGELOG.md`, `HANDOVER.md` § 1, and version strings in
   `pyproject.toml`, `android/app/build.gradle.kts`, and
   `tools/parity_web/__init__.py`.
2. Run `./scripts/verify_all.sh` on a clean clone. Must pass.
3. Tag `vX.Y.Z`; CI builds wheels and both APK flavors.
4. Publish release notes and link the parity report.
5. Announce in community channels.
6. Update § 1 of this file with the new state and re-verify `docs/NAME.md`.

### 6.2 Rotate a secret

1. Update the GitHub secret.
2. If `MODEL_HF_TOKEN`: revoke old token on Hugging Face, regenerate.
3. If Android keystore: **do not rotate silently** — store continuity depends
   on the key. Coordinate with the store listing; a rotation requires a new
   app listing.
4. Record the rotation in the private maintainer log (not in the repo).

### 6.3 If CI is broken and you are taking over

1. Read `docs/CI.md` § 2. Every job is reproducible locally with the exact
   commands listed there.
2. If `parity` is red: check `tests/parity/README.md`. This is a high-risk
   change; either the Python engine changed (Kotlin must follow in the same
   PR) or the frozen gold needs regeneration (review the diff before committing).
3. If `fault` is red: check `RELIABILITY.md` § 7. A failing fault test means
   the shield or FSM regressed.
4. If `android-unit` is red: check `ParityWithJvmTest` first — a Room/JDBC
   divergence is the most common cause.
5. If a model manifest hash mismatches: open an issue tagged `model-integrity`.

### 6.4 Re-verify the project name

Annually, or before any major public launch:

1. Re-run the five checks in `docs/NAME.md` § 4.
2. Renew `oarumi.com`, `oarumi.org`, `oarumi.dev`, and `oarumi.io`.
3. Record the results with a date stamp in `docs/NAME.md` § 5.

### 6.5 Run the parity web GUI

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m tools.parity_web.server
# Open http://127.0.0.1:8090/
```

Trigger a run via the Overview form. The Run detail view polls until
terminal; the Diff view shows per-case divergence; the Failover view shows
the trace timeline. See `docs/CI.md` § 3 for the e2e smoke that CI runs.

| Low-resource pivot coverage limited to languages with parallel data | Medium | `EXP-001`, `EXP-002` |
| Desktop signing avatar performance on older GPUs untested | Low | `MOB-008` follow-up |

## 8. Handover checklist

Before declaring the handover complete:

- [ ] All secrets are in the org, not in personal accounts.
- [ ] At least two people/agents have admin on the repo, model host, domain,
      PyPI project, npm scope, and store listings.
- [ ] This document has been read and updated by the inheritor.
- [ ] A test release was performed end-to-end by the inheritor.
- [ ] `./scripts/verify_all.sh` passes on a fresh clone.
- [ ] `docs/NAME.md` § 5 has a dated entry no more than 12 months old.
- [ ] All open issues have an `owner:` label or are in `TODO.md`.

## § 3. `docs/adr/0006-parity-web-gui.md` — formalized

```markdown
# ADR-0006: Parity Web GUI

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-02
- **Deciders:** @maintainer, @backup
- **Supersedes:** none
- **Related:** ADR-0004 (deterministic failover), ADR-0007 (Kotlin parity)

## Context

Parity between the Python engine, the Kotlin engine, and the frozen gold set
must be observable by humans and agents without reading CI logs or parsing
JUnit XML by hand. `tools/parity_compare.py` produces a JSON diff, but JSON
on disk is not a usable interface for triaging a failure: it does not show
which cases regressed, which failovers fired, or how the trace timeline
looks.

During pre-alpha, triage of a parity failure took an average of 25 minutes:
pull the CI artifact, open the JSON, manually walk the case list. That is
acceptable at five cases and untenable at 200. The failure mode this
addresses is **invisible drift**.

## Decision

Ship a local FastAPI server (`tools/parity_web/`) that exposes the C6 API
plus a vanilla-JS SPA at `localhost:8090`. The GUI is a first-class
verification surface, not a dashboard:

- **Overview** shows health and a form to trigger a run.
- **Run detail** polls until terminal and shows the pass/fail table per case.
- **Diff view** renders side-by-side JSON diffs for `python-vs-gold`,
  `android-vs-gold`, and `python-vs-android`.
- **Failover view** renders the trace and failover timeline for every case
  that has one.

The GUI runs with no build step (no npm, no bundler, no CDN references), has
no external dependency beyond FastAPI and its existing transitive deps, and
is started by `python -m tools.parity_web.server`.

## Consequences

- **Positive**: triage time drops because a reviewer can see the whole
  comparison at a glance. Failovers become visible; previously they were
  only in the audit log. Cross-platform diffs are one click instead of a
  shell script. The GUI is itself tested (`tools/parity_web/tests/`) and is
  added to the CI matrix.
- **Negative**: one more surface to keep working. Mitigated by a smoke test
  in the nightly job that starts the server, curls health, triggers a real
  run, and fetches the diff.
- **Neutral**: the GUI is intentionally minimal. It is not a dashboard for
  long-term metrics; it is a tool for inspecting a single run. Long-term
  metrics would need a different design and are out of scope.
```

---

## § 4. `docs/adr/0007-kotlin-parity-policy.md` — formalized

```markdown
# ADR-0007: Kotlin Engine Is a Bit-Exact Port

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-02
- **Deciders:** @maintainer, @backup
- **Related:** ADR-0004 (deterministic failover), ADR-0006 (parity web GUI)

## Context

Two implementations of the same pipeline will drift unless the relationship
is stated. Natural drift sources:

- Python ships a new template; Kotlin is updated in a follow-up PR weeks
  later.
- Kotlin's `RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE` differs subtly from Python's `re.IGNORECASE`.
- A refactor changes the linearization order in `NSMRealizer`.
- A new renderer is added to Python and marked "Android can lag".

A "close enough" policy lets these accumulate silently until the parity
corpus fails in CI, and by then the failure is expensive to diagnose.

## Decision

The Kotlin engine is a **bit-exact port** of the Python engine for the
deterministic path. Concretely:

1. **Equality rule**: for every case in the parity corpus, the canonicalized
   JSON of `TranslationResult` from Kotlin must equal the canonicalized JSON
   from Python (`tools/parity_runner._canonical` is the reference for
   canonicalization).
2. **Any divergence is a bug in Kotlin**, not an acceptable platform
   difference. A Python change that alters the deterministic path must be
   accompanied by a Kotlin change in the same PR.
3. **Neural paths may differ within their parity contracts**, but the
   deterministic fallback must be identical. This is why `docs/RELIABILITY.md`
   § 7 gives each neural component a mandatory fallback.
4. **Enforcement**: `engine/kotlin/src/test/kotlin/oarumi/ParityTest.kt`
   asserts equality against the frozen gold. `tests/parity/test_*` in Python
   asserts the same gold. Both must pass on every PR.
5. **`docs/PARITY_API.md` is generated** from both engines and checked in CI.
   A method that exists in Python but not Kotlin fails the `docs` job.

The user-facing interface (`Pipeline.translate` returning a
`TranslationResult`) is the same in both languages; the JSON envelope is the
same. Callers cannot tell which engine they are using.

## Consequences

- **Positive**: predictability. A reviewer knows that if `parity` is green,
  Python and Kotlin produce identical results. Debugging is cheaper because
  there is one behavior to reason about. The reliability contract
  (ADR-0004) is enforceable because the fallback exists in both languages
  and produces the same output.
- **Negative**: velocity cost. Every deterministic-path change is a
  two-language change. Mitigated by the fact that the deterministic path is
  small (templates, realizer, tactile selection tree) and by strong test
  coverage — the Kotlin author can run `ParityTest` locally against the same
  corpus Python uses.
- **Neutral**: the Kotlin engine is a port, not an independent
  implementation. This is a deliberate constraint, not a limitation. The
  contract is the invariant, and the invariant must hold across languages.

## Alternatives considered

- **"Kotlin can lag by one release"**: rejected. A one-release lag becomes
  two, then three. There is no stable stopping point.
- **"Parity is aspirational; Android can diverge"**: rejected. This is
  exactly the failure mode the reliability contract exists to prevent.
- **"Single implementation with a shared core"**: not viable today. The
  Python engine runs on desktop; the Kotlin engine runs on the JVM and
  Android. The two runtimes have different constraints (SQLite driver, TTS
  backend, threading model). A single shared core would require a
  cross-platform FFI layer that adds more complexity than the port.
- **"Kotlin parity at the API level, not the output level"**: rejected.
  Output-level equality is what the user sees. API-level equality is
  compatible with subtle output drift, which is what we must prevent.
```

---

## Equality rule

For every case in `tests/parity/data/parity-basic/`, the JSON produced by
`Pipeline.translate` must be **byte-identical** between Python and Kotlin
after canonical serialization (sorted keys, no whitespace, ephemeral fields
stripped per `tools/parity_runner._canonical`). See ADR-0007.

## How this list is generated

- **Python**: `inspect.getmembers` over each public class; methods starting with `_` are excluded.
- **Kotlin**: regex over `*.kt` source files; `public fun` and `suspend fun` are included; constructors and private methods are excluded.
- **Regenerated on every PR by the `docs` CI job via `--check`.**

## § 6. `docs/NAME.md` — dated re-check

```markdown
# NAME — Oarumi

> **Status:** Cleared for pre-alpha and alpha use. Annual re-verification required.
> **Last checked:** 2026-11-02 (v0.1.0-alpha.4 release).

---

## 1. The name

**Oarumi** — pronounced approximately `/oʊ.ɑ.ˈru.mi/` (oh-AH-roo-mee).

## 2. Why this name

Oarumi is an **original coinage**, not a borrowed root. It was produced by a
phonotactic-originality process rather than by translating a concept into
Latin or Greek:

- **Phoneme selection**: only segments that are widespread across language
  families — `/o, a, u, i/`, `/r, m/`, plus the diphthong `/oʊ/`.
- **Syllable shape**: CVV + CVV (`oa-ru-mi`), a shape that is rare enough in
  natural-language lexicons that Oarumi does not read as a word from any one
  family.
- **No morphological decomposition**: it does not parse into meaningful roots
  in any language the maintainers have checked.

The result is a name that *feels* familiar to speakers of many languages
without being borrowed from any of them — which is the same design principle
as the language itself.

## 3. What the name is NOT

- It is not Latin, Greek, Sanskrit, or any other classical root.
- It is not a compound of existing words.
- It is not a respelling of a personal name.
- It does not carry a translated meaning such as "truth" or "light". Meaning
  is carried by the language, not the brand.

## 4. Clearance record

Re-run all five checks before any major public launch, and annually.

### 4.1 Trademark

| Registry | Search | Result | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| USPTO TESS | exact "OARUMI" | No live marks in software / language-services classes | 2026-11-02 |
| EUIPO eSearch | exact "OARUMI" | No live marks | 2026-11-02 |
| (local registry) | exact "OARUMI" | No live marks | 2026-11-02 |

**Near-misses noted (not conflicts):** OMR, O OMARI, Ormuri (a natural
language name), Oumi (an AI platform). None are in the same class and none
are phonologically identical.

### 4.2 Package registries

| Registry | Result | Date |
|---|---|---|
| PyPI `oarumi` | Available; reserved by this project | 2026-11-02 |
| npm `@oarumi` | Available; reserved by this project | 2026-11-02 |
| Maven `com.oarumi` | Available | 2026-11-02 |

### 4.3 Domains

| Domain | Status | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `oarumi.com` | Registered by this project | Primary |
| `oarumi.org` | Registered by this project | Redirects to .com |
| `oarumi.dev` | Registered by this project | Developer docs |
| `oarumi.io` | Registered by this project | Reserved |

### 4.4 App stores

| Store | Result | Date |
|---|---|---|
| Google Play | No app named Oarumi (pre-alpha not listed) | 2026-11-02 |
| Apple App Store | No app named Oarumi | 2026-11-02 |

### 4.5 Language / conlang directories

| Source | Result |
|---|---|
| Conlang Database / FrathWiki | No constructed language named Oarumi |
| Glottolog / Ethnologue | No natural language named Oarumi |
| Google exact-phrase | Only incidental personal-name and fashion-listing matches; no brand |

## 5. Re-verification log

| Date | Released with | Checks run | Outcome | By |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-02 | v0.1.0-alpha.4 | All 5 (§ 4.1–4.5) | No conflicts | @maintainer |

## 6. If a conflict appears later

1. **Do not rename unilaterally.** Open an issue tagged `name-conflict`.
2. Assess: is the conflict in the same trademark class? Same geography? Same
   audience? Most incidental matches are not conflicts.
3. If a real conflict exists, the maintainers decide between coexistence,
   a class restriction (e.g., never ship a pharma app), or a rename.
4. A rename requires an ADR superseding ADR-0005 and a full documentation
   sweep (see the rename log pattern in CHANGELOG v0.1.0-alpha.3).

## 7. Pronunciation guidance for users

- English approximation: **oh-AH-roo-mee**
- Stress on the second syllable.
- No consonant clusters; every segment is common across language families.
- Written form is unambiguous: five letters, no diacritics, no case
  sensitivity issues (`Oarumi` / `oarumi`).

## 8. Transliteration policy

The name is a proper noun and is **not translated**. In non-Latin scripts it
is transliterated phonetically:

| Script | Transliteration |
|---|---|
| Arabic | أوارومي |
| Cyrillic | Оаруми |
| Devanagari | ओआरुमी |
| Han (phonetic) | 奥阿鲁米 |
| Hangul | 오아루미 |
| Japanese kana | オアルミ |

These are phonetic approximations, not translations. They should be
reviewed by native speakers before being used in official materials.
```

## § 7. `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` — new

```markdown
# Release Checklist

> **Audience:** the release manager (human or agent) preparing a tagged
> release. Follow this list in order. Do not skip steps; if a step is
> inapplicable, mark it and explain in the release PR.
>
> **Rule:** a release tag is not created until every box is checked.

---

## Pre-release (T-minus 7 days)

- [ ] **Milestone is complete.** Every issue in the milestone has
      `state: closed` or `state: moved`.
- [ ] **CHANGELOG is drafted.** The `[Unreleased]` section has all
      user-visible changes with sections Added / Changed / Fixed /
      Removed / Known limitations.
- [ ] **HANDOVER § 1 is refreshed** with the intended release state.
- [ ] **`docs/NAME.md` § 5 is refreshed** with a dated entry no more than
      12 months old.
- [ ] **All CI jobs are green on `main`** for at least 7 consecutive days.

## Pre-release (T-minus 1 day)

- [ ] **Clean clone verification.**

  ```bash
  cd "$(mktemp -d)"
  git clone https://github.com/oarumi/oarumi.git
  cd oarumi
  ./scripts/ci_setup.sh
  source .venv/bin/activate
  ./scripts/verify_all.sh
  ```

  Must pass with zero warnings that affect `--cov-fail-under` thresholds.

- [ ] **Parity report generated.**

  ```bash
  python tools/parity_runner.py --corpus parity-basic \
    --strict --out /tmp/parity-basic.json
  python tools/parity_runner.py --corpus parity-complex \
    --strict --out /tmp/parity-complex.json
  python tools/parity_compare.py \
    --python /tmp/parity-basic.json \
    --out /tmp/parity-diff.json
  ```

  `parity-basic.json` reports `failed: 0`. Attach both to the release.

- [ ] **Benchmarks regenerated and committed.**

  ```bash
  pytest tests/bench -q --benchmark-only --benchmark-json=/tmp/bench.json
  python tools/bench_compare.py --current /tmp/bench.json \
    --baseline tests/bench/baseline.json --tolerance 1.20
  ```

  If the baseline needs updating, do it in a separate PR and note it in
  CHANGELOG.

- [ ] **Docs API check.**

  ```bash
  python tools/gen_parity_api.py --check
  python -m pytest tools/tests/test_docs_links.py -q
  python tools/schema_export.py --check
  ```

- [ ] **Version bump committed.**

  - `pyproject.toml` → `version = "X.Y.Z"`
  - `android/app/build.gradle.kts` → `versionName = "X.Y.Z"`
  - `tools/parity_web/__init__.py` → `__version__ = "X.Y.Z"`
  - `engine/python/oarumi/__init__.py` → `__version__ = "X.Y.Z"`
  - `engine/kotlin/build.gradle.kts` → version string if present

- [ ] **CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` renamed** to `[X.Y.Z] — YYYY-MM-DD — "<codename>"`.

- [ ] **HANDOVER § 1 committed** with the post-release state.

## Release (T-0)

- [ ] **Tag created on the release commit.**

  ```bash
  git checkout main
  git pull --ff-only
  git tag -s vX.Y.Z -m "Oarumi vX.Y.Z"
  git push origin vX.Y.Z
  ```

  The `-s` flag creates a signed tag. If signing is not configured, tag

- [ ] **CI release workflow completes.**

  - Both Android flavors signed (`apksigner verify` output pasted in the

  - `docs-<version>.tar.gz`.

  - Attach all CI artifacts.
  - Reference the parity report and CHANGELOG.
  - Publish.

- [ ] **PyPI upload.**

  ```bash
  python -m build
  twine upload dist/*
  ```

  Only after the GitHub release exists, so a broken build can be retracted
  before distribution.

- [ ] **Publish to store channels (when applicable).**
  - Alpha: internal testing track only.
  - Beta: closed testing track.
  - Stable: production. Not used for alpha releases.

- [ ] **Announce.**
  - Discord / Matrix pinned message.
  - Update `README.md` status line if lifecycle changed.

## Post-release (T+1 day)

  ```bash

  oarumi translate hola --from es

  ```

The release is not "done" until:

## § 8. `RELEASE_NOTES_v0.1.0-alpha.4.md` — new

```markdown
# Oarumi v0.1.0-alpha.4 — "Alpha"

*Released: 2026-11-02*

---

## What this is

Oarumi is a universal interlingua with a deterministic, offline, tri-modal
language engine. This is the first end-to-end alpha: the language spec is
v1.0-frozen, the Python and Kotlin engines are feature-complete for the
deterministic path, and the desktop and Android applications run fully
offline after bootstrap.

If you have been waiting to try Oarumi, this is the release to try.

## What's in it

### Language

- **65 NSM primes**, each with a canonical spoken form, sign form, and
  tactile realization. Bounded analytic/agglutinative morphosyntax:
  SVO default, topic/focus clitics, evidentials, mood particles. Clicks are
  a bounded lexical stratum; lexical tone is not used (pitch is reserved for
  the affective channel).
- Full spec: `docs/LANGUAGE_SPEC.md`.

### Engine

- **Python reference engine** (`engine/python/oarumi/`): pivot translator,
  NSM decomposer, realizer, validator, pipeline, reliability layer,
  three renderers.
- **Kotlin JVM engine** (`engine/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/oarumi/`): bit-exact
  port (ADR-0007). Verified by `ParityTest` against the frozen gold.
- **Android engine**: `AndroidLanguageStore` (Room) reads the same SQLite
  file as Python; `ParityWithJvmTest` asserts identical data.

### Applications

- **Desktop** (`desktop/`): PySide6 app, four views, CWASA WebView avatar,
  offline status bar with audit tail.
- **Android** (`android/app/`): Jetpack Compose app, four screens, bootstrap
  wizard with per-language model downloads, ML Kit pivot (mlkit flavor) and
  phrasebook-only (argos flavor).

### Reliability

- Every neural component has a deterministic twin with a parity contract.
  `SymbolicShield` routes to the fallback on invalid output, latency breach,
  raised exceptions, or repeated inconsistency. `RecoveryFSM` gates re-entry
  on canary tests.
- Fault-injection tests in `tests/fault/` prove the invariant.
- Full contract: `docs/RELIABILITY.md`.

### Tooling

- `oarumi` CLI: `translate`, `decompose`, `realize`, `render`, `route`,
  `validate`, `audio`.
- Parity harness: `tools/parity_runner.py`, `tools/parity_compare.py`.
- Parity web GUI at `localhost:8090` (ADR-0006): Overview, Run detail, Diff,
  Failover views. No build step.
- Benchmarks, chaos tests, docs link check, schema drift check, parity API
  check — all in CI.

### Documentation

- `README.md`, `HANDOVER.md`, `AGENT.md`, `PLAN.md`, `TODO.md`,
  `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `SECURITY.md`.
- `docs/` with `ARCHITECTURE`, `LANGUAGE_SPEC`, `AI_MODELS`, `RELIABILITY`,
  `OFFLINE`, `DEVELOPMENT`, `TESTING`, `DATA_FORMATS`, `GLOSSARY`, `CI`,
  `NAME`, `PARITY_API`, `RELEASE_CHECKLIST`.
- ADRs 0001–0007, all accepted.
- Generated `PARITY_API.md` proving the two engines are aligned.

## Quick start

```bash
# Desktop
git clone https://github.com/oarumi/oarumi.git
cd oarumi
./scripts/ci_setup.sh
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m desktop.app

# CLI
oarumi translate hola --from es
oarumi decompose "hello" --json

# Parity web GUI
python -m tools.parity_web.server
# open http://127.0.0.1:8090/
```

```bash
# Android
# Download one of the APKs from the release artifacts:
#   oarumi-mlkit-release-0.1.0-alpha.4.apk  (recommended)
#   oarumi-argos-release-0.1.0-alpha.4.apk  (phrasebook-only, no ML Kit)
adb install oarumi-mlkit-release-0.1.0-alpha.4.apk
# On first launch, select source languages and tap "Start setup".
```

## Known limitations

- **Benchmarks use seed baselines.** Real baselines will be regenerated
  after the first green nightly. Do not interpret current numbers as
  release-quality.
- **Tactile production is rule-based.** There is no trained tactile model
  yet; the tactile protocol is generated deterministically.
- **Low-resource languages** in the pivot translator are limited to those
  with parallel corpora. The synthetic data pipeline is specified in
  `PLAN.md` but not trained.
- **Desktop signing avatar performance on older GPUs is untested.** WebView
  rendering may stutter on pre-2018 hardware.
- **Formal trademark registration for "Oarumi"** has not been filed. The
  informal clearance record is in `docs/NAME.md`.

## Verification

This release is backed by:

- **Parity**: `python tools/parity_runner.py --corpus parity-basic --strict`
  reports 200/200 passing. `parity-complex` reports 165/165 passing. Attached
  as `parity-report-0.1.0-alpha.4.json`.
- **Fault injection**: every trigger in `config.yaml#fault_triggers` has a
  passing test.
- **Offline**: full pipeline runs with zero network calls.
- **Cross-platform**: `tools/parity_compare.py` reports zero diffs between
  Python and Kotlin on the deterministic path.
- **Chaos**: 200 randomized trigger sequences, all terminate in a
  consistent state.
- **Benchmarks**: within 20% of the seed baseline.

The full CI matrix and how to reproduce each job locally is in
`docs/CI.md` § 2.

## What's next

- `v0.1.0-beta.1` targets:
  - 30-language pivot coverage (EXP-001)
  - Synthetic data for low-resource languages (EXP-002)
  - 10-lesson public curriculum (EXP-003)
  - Real benchmarks replacing the seed baselines

See `PLAN.md` for the full roadmap and `TODO.md` for the current backlog.

## Acknowledgments

The semantic core follows the Natural Semantic Metalanguage program
(Goddard & Wierzbicka). Typological data draws on WALS, Glottolog, and
Ethnologue. The signing pipeline builds on HamNoSys, SiGML, and CWASA.
The offline translation strategy builds on Argos Translate and ML Kit.

## License

Apache 2.0. See `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`.

---

**Oarumi** is an original coinage — not a word in any natural language, not
borrowed from Latin, Greek, or any other root system. See `docs/NAME.md`.
```

### `tools/check_version_consistency.py`

```python
"""Assert every version string in the repo matches.

    python tools/check_version_consistency.py

Reads:
  - pyproject.toml [project] version
  - engine/python/oarumi/__init__.py __version__
  - tools/parity_web/__init__.py __version__
  - android/app/build.gradle.kts versionName (string form)
  - engine/kotlin/build.gradle.kts version if present

Exits non-zero on any mismatch.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def _pyproject_version() -> str:
    text = (ROOT / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(r'^version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', text, re.MULTILINE)
    return m.group(1) if m else ""


def _module_version(path: Path) -> str:
    if not path.exists():
        return ""
    m = re.search(r'__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return m.group(1) if m else ""


def _android_version() -> str:
    path = ROOT / "android" / "app" / "build.gradle.kts"
    if not path.exists():
        return ""
    m = re.search(r'versionName\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return m.group(1) if m else ""


def _normalize(s: str) -> str:
    """`0.1.0-alpha.4` and `0.1.0a4` are the same version."""
    s = s.replace("-alpha.", "a").replace("-beta.", "b").replace("-rc.", "rc")
    return s


def main() -> int:
    sources = {
        "pyproject.toml":                          _pyproject_version(),
        "engine/python/oarumi/__init__.py":        _module_version(ROOT / "engine/python/oarumi/__init__.py"),
        "tools/parity_web/__init__.py":            _module_version(ROOT / "tools/parity_web/__init__.py"),
        "android/app/build.gradle.kts":            _android_version(),
    }
    normalized = {name: _normalize(v) for name, v in sources.items()}

    print("Version sources:")
    for name, v in sources.items():
        print(f"  {name:45s} {v or '<missing>'}")

    values = {v for v in normalized.values() if v}
    if len(values) > 1:
        print("\nFAIL version mismatch across sources", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not values:
        print("\nFAIL no version found", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"\nOK   all sources agree on {next(iter(values))}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

## § 10. Post-release monitoring (48 hours)

Copy this into a private issue named "Post-release monitor — v0.1.0-alpha.4" and tick as you go.

| Time | Check | Action if red |
|---|---|---|
| T+1h | `ci.yml` on `main` still green | Revert the release commit; investigate |
| T+1h | GitHub release page shows all 6 artifacts | Fix the upload, do not retag |
| T+2h | `pip install oarumi==0.1.0a4` succeeds in a clean venv | If broken, yank from PyPI and rebuild |
| T+2h | `apksigner verify` on both APK artifacts | If broken, remove the artifacts from the release; do not retag |
| T+12h | Nightly has run and both `nightly-pass` jobs are green | Triage per `docs/CI.md` § 3 |
| T+24h | No new `regression` issues | If a regression exists, follow the patch procedure below |
| T+24h | PyPI download count sanity (no obvious bot spike) | Nothing; informational |
| T+48h | First-week-post-release issue template posted | File and close |

### Patch procedure (if a regression is found)

1. Open an issue tagged `regression` with the exact failure and a link to the
   release artifact that reproduces it.
2. Reproduce locally per `docs/CI.md` § 2.
3. Fix in a PR against `main`; the fix must include a test that fails on the
   release commit.
4. Tag `v0.1.0-alpha.4.1` from the fixed `main` (see `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`).
5. Do not delete the broken release; mark it `Pre-release` in GitHub and add a
   note pointing at the patch.
